prize_parts.citation: For energy-landscape theory of protein folding and the experimental mapping of folding pathways and transition states

statement.case_for: I keep B027 as my position, for a reason of scientific content and not of counting. The funnelled energy landscape is a physical statement about biomolecules: a minimally frustrated sequence has a landscape biased toward the native state, so folding is fast, barriers are small and pathways can be heterogeneous. That is a quantitative, falsifiable picture linking statistical mechanics to kinetics, and decades of simulation, kinetic experiments and single-molecule work have tested it. Fersht's protein-engineering and phi-value analysis is the experimental method that made transition states visible, so the prize would honour theory and the experiments that could test it, in one coherent story. The 2024 prize rewarded predicting and designing structures; it did not explain why a sequence folds at all, and the two are complementary. The attribution is the most compact among the mature mechanistic candidates: Wolynes and Onuchic for the funnel and its formalism, Fersht for the experimental foundation.
statement.case_against: Round 1 sharpened the weaknesses. Bryngelson and Dill have real priority claims on frustration and the landscape picture, and the three-name limit forces an exclusion that the expert reports must justify. Pairing theory with experiment is a choice, and the chair is right to ask whether it is one discovery or two. Support is narrow: one first place in the opening and one stated preference in round 1, so B027 cannot claim breadth. Sparr and Linke argue that the funnel language mostly restates what folding kinetics had already shown and that the 2024 prize reduces the appetite for another folding prize. The funnel is also more a unifying framework than a single decisive result, which fits poorly with a committee that values clearly attributable discoveries.

responses.point: The chair asks what the funnel picture predicted that folding kinetics did not already show, and whether the 2024 prize reduces the case for B027, and he asks whether the citation honours theory, experiment or both.
responses.response: The picture earns its place through what it explains beyond a list of kinetic measurements: why folding is not a random search, why small proteins fold on microsecond to millisecond times with few intermediates, why topology and native-state contacts set rates, and why transition states are broad ensembles that phi-values probe. I will not claim more than the expert reports can support, and I would want them to say which of these statements were predictions made before the data. On the 2024 prize, the structure of the question differs: that prize answered what the structure of a sequence is, and the funnel answers why the sequence reaches it. On the citation, I would honour both, and word it so that Fersht is credited for the experimental method that tested the landscape, not as an add-on. If the reports show the two cannot be one discovery, I would revisit the trio. I also note your own chair observation that B022 rests on the in-cell question; I keep B022 out of my alternatives for that reason.

responses.point: Chabes argues that PROTACs and cereblon-mediated glues are one mechanism, redirection of an E3 ligase to a new substrate, so a single citation naming Crews, Deshaies and Handa can cover both.
responses.response: I take the mechanistic argument seriously, and it is the best case I have seen for treating B068 as one achievement. The chemical logic of induced proximity is shared. Where I still differ is on what the committee can document. The PROTAC concept and the discovery that thalidomide-type drugs act through cereblon have different origins, different structural biology and different clinical histories, and a citation that spans both leaves Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim to be explained. The lack of an approved degrader also weighs for me as a question of timing, not of validity. I move B068 up as my first alternative, but I would not make it my preferred part until the reports separate the chemical insight from the clinical pipeline and settle whether Handa or Ciulli holds the third place.

responses.point: Somfai holds that Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the cleanest case on maturity and attribution, with Buchwald and Hartwig as a two-person prize and a distinct mechanistic problem (amine binding, C-N reductive elimination).
responses.response: In round 1 I asked what new chemical understanding C-N coupling gave beyond the 2010 prize. Your answer, together with Zou's, is that the C-N bond required its own ligand and mechanistic solution, and that is a fair scientific argument, not only an argument from utility. I now list B057 among my alternatives for that reason. I still want the reports to show that the mechanistic advance is a separate discovery and not a sequel, and I agree with you that Kosugi and Migita should be acknowledged in the background text, since the citation can say general and catalytic without erasing them. I do not move B057 to first place, because I judge a mechanism-level principle in a biological system to have more reach, but I recognise that the committee may prefer the clearest attribution.

responses.point: Sparr ranks energy-landscape theory among her alternatives but says it has been less directly tested than the condensate work, and she raises the overlap with the 2024 prize and Bryngelson and Dill priority.
responses.response: I disagree on the testing. Phi-value analysis, folding-rate studies across many proteins, single-molecule experiments and large-scale simulation have repeatedly confronted the landscape picture, whereas for condensates the in-cell question you yourself list as unresolved remains open. I do accept your point on priority. If the expert reports show that Bryngelson and Dill hold the origin of the frustration concept, the credit would need reconsidering, and I would then ask whether a two-name theory prize would serve better than the trio. I do not think the committee should treat B027 as less mature than B022; on the evidence now in this exchange, it is the more mature of the two.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports assign the minimal-frustration and funnel concepts to Wolynes and Onuchic, or whether Bryngelson and Dill must displace a name.
Whether the committee will accept theory plus experiment as one prize part, given the chair's question.
Whether B027, with one stated preference, can draw the five votes needed, or whether the committee will consolidate on B068, B057 or B022.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader is a timing matter that justifies waiting on B068.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent for B027, B068, B057 or B022: none of the credited names appears in my profile. I remain a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou and a long-time colleague of Johan Aqvist, which the chair noted, and I do not regard it as bearing on any shortlisted candidate. No recusal is indicated.
